title: Joseph's seven-year famine
summary: CFAH AP-58: Joseph's famine 1708–1701 BC (with the Senusret I Year 25 low Nile and the Unas famine). Ussher dates the start of the famine to 1708 BC.
description: The seven years of famine foretold by Joseph (Gen 41:30, 53-57). Jacob came down to Egypt in its second year (Gen 45:6). CFAH-6 aligns it with a low Nile in Year 25 of Senusret I and the famine relief shown in the causeway of Unas.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 6: The Old and Middle Kingdoms of Egypt," ARJ 18 (2025): 13–60, Argument 2, Table 1 "Anchor Points for early Egyptian history" #58; Argument 4 §8 "Joseph's Famine 1708–1701, Senusret I Year 25 Low Nile, Unas Famine"
chronologies.note: CFAH-6 Table 1: "Joseph's Famine, Senusret I Famine, Unas Famine"

chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Third Age §133 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
chronologies.note: Seven years of plenty ended; the famine began (Gen 41:53-54). Ussher's §133 header places it in 1708 BC.
Jones (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament, 2002) gives no date for this extra-biblical event.

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 5, chart "Chronology From Abraham’s Death to Joseph’s Death"
chronologies.note: The compilation gives only the end of the famine (AM 2303); by Gen 45:6 the descent (2298) was in its second year.
